newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds down in the dumps after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds down in the dumps after quiet day.

text.p: German Bunds failed to pull themselves out of negative territory on Monday as a lack of impetus left trade quiet.
Traders said the DTB September Bund future was fenced into a 10-tick range in late session trade after failing to take on strong technical resistance at 101.50/56.
By 1510 GMT, the contract was trading nine basis points lower on the day at 101.25, having visited a low at 101.08 and a high at 101.45 during the session.
Weakness in the U.S. Treasury market was also dampening sentiment, traders said.
Domestic data showing a slight tick-up in May inflation in the state of Bavaria was also slightly disappointing but had little impact on the market, analysts said.
The government's issuance calendar, while as expected, sparked some nervousness.
Bonn said it planned to issue 41 billion marks of debt in the third quarter, including around 10 billion marks of 30-year bonds. It is the first 30-year issue in more than three years.
"One can't help but have a slightly uncomfortable feeling," said Trinkaus Capital Management bond analyst Frank Schroeder.
He said players were concerned that if the government had locked itself into current rates for 30 years, the scope for any easing in monetary policy in the future was very limited.
Looking ahead, analysts said the market was likely to remain subdued, hoping to consolidate with little in the way of data on the horizon.

Consumer confidence data due from the U.S. at 1400 GMT are expected to show a slight setback in mood, with the index forecast to fall to 126.3 in May from 127.1 in April. This could help Bunds gains some strength, traders said.
